heuristics.rule: Ask the advisor's internship philosophy before committing — it immediately reveals which track they optimize for
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a prospective PhD advisor for an industry research career...
heuristics.action: ...ask directly: 'What's your philosophy on PhD student internships?' and listen for whether they proactively name companies vs. express reluctance
heuristics.because: An advisor who views internships as disruptions creates a structural disadvantage for industry placement regardless of program rank or advisor reputation

heuristics.rule: Use LinkedIn to verify where an advisor's students actually interned — not where the advisor claims connections
heuristics.condition: When an advisor claims industry connections or a pipeline to top AI labs...
heuristics.action: ...search LinkedIn for the advisor's past PhD students and trace their actual internship history
heuristics.because: Claimed connections are cheap; verifiable placement history (Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta AI) is the authoritative signal of real pipeline access

heuristics.rule: For academic-track PhDs, program rank matters more than advisor fit; for industry-track PhDs, advisor industry connections matter more than program rank
heuristics.condition: When choosing between a higher-ranked program with a less connected advisor vs. a lower-ranked program with an advisor who has strong industry lab relationships...
heuristics.action: ...weight program rank heavily if targeting faculty positions, weight advisor industry connections heavily if targeting research scientist roles
heuristics.because: Academic hiring is top-heavy and credential-driven by institution; industry research hiring is relationship- and internship-pipeline-driven

heuristics.rule: If your actual goal is SWE, do not pursue a PhD — calculate the opportunity cost explicitly before applying
heuristics.condition: When a student is considering a PhD primarily to improve competitiveness for software engineering roles...
heuristics.action: ...calculate the 4–5 year opportunity cost ($500,000–$600,000 pretax) against the marginal or negative PhD premium for SWE roles
heuristics.because: PhD SWEs and MS SWEs are compensated identically at the same level at most companies, and PhD candidates may be filtered as overqualified

heuristics.rule: Investigate co-supervision PhD programs at target industry labs before defaulting to a standard university PhD
heuristics.condition: When a student's target employer is a major AI lab (Google, Meta AI, Microsoft Research, OpenAI)...
heuristics.action: ...research whether that lab has a formal PhD co-supervision or residency program before choosing a standard academic program
heuristics.because: Co-supervision programs offer faster publication timelines, more applied research, and supplemented compensation — a structurally different and often superior path for industry research goals

heuristics.rule: Ask for the placement list of the last 5 PhD graduates, not general claims about program quality
heuristics.condition: When evaluating any PhD program during visit days...
heuristics.action: ...ask specifically: 'Where did your last 5 PhD graduates go?' and assess the ratio and quality of academic vs. industry placements
heuristics.because: Aggregate program reputation lags current advisor-specific placement reality; recent concrete placements are more predictive than rankings

decision_factors.factor: Target career track (academic vs. industry research vs. SWE)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The optimal program, advisor, and strategy differ fundamentally across tracks — optimizing for the wrong track wastes years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Honestly identify whether you want a faculty position, a research scientist role, or a software engineering role before applying — these are not equivalent endpoints

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The advisor's network and track record directly determine internship access, letter quality, and job placement probability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: LinkedIn search of past PhD students for internship history and post-graduation roles; ask directly which companies students have interned at in the last 3 years

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Matters significantly for academic track (top-5/10 programs dominate faculty placements); matters less for industry research track where advisor connections can compensate
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check assistant professor placement data by program; for industry track, rank-30 with strong industry advisor can outperform rank-10 with no industry connections

decision_factors.why_it_matters: An advisor who discourages internships structurally disadvantages industry-track students regardless of other program strengths
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly during visits; listen for specificity (names companies) vs. vagueness or discouragement

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's industry research partnerships and consulting relationships
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Active industry collaborations create internship pipelines, co-authored publications with industry researchers, and warm introductions to hiring managers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'Do you have active research collaborations with industry labs? Which ones?' and verify against advisor's recent publications and acknowledgments

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Industry demand and academic job market competitiveness vary dramatically by subfield — ML/AI has extreme industry demand but also the most competitive academic market; theory has moderate industry demand
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference the subfield table: ML/AI/NLP have highest industry demand; theory has moderate industry demand; HCI has moderate demand in both tracks

decision_factors.factor: Existence of formal co-supervision programs at target industry labs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Represents a structurally distinct and potentially superior path for industry research goals — faster timelines, supplemented compensation, applied research
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research Google Brain Residency, Meta AI Research programs, Microsoft Research PhD fellowships, OpenAI collaborations before defaulting to standard programs

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's h-index and academic network breadth (for academic track)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Authoritative recommendation letters from well-networked advisors are a prerequisite for competitive academic hiring committee access
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check h-index in the subfield; ask how many hiring committee relationships the advisor has across institutions; assess grant history for funding runway

decision_factors.factor: Opportunity cost calculation (especially for SWE-bound students)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 4–5 years of stipend ($32K–$40K/yr) vs. industry SWE salary ($150K–$200K/yr) represents $500K–$600K pretax foregone earnings
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate explicitly: multiply years-in-program by delta between stipend and market SWE salary; compare against realistic PhD premium for target role

decision_factors.factor: Teaching assistant experience (academic vs. industry track)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: TA experience is an asset for academic track (demonstrates teaching competency for faculty applications); it is not a meaningful differentiator for industry research roles
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether TA requirements serve or distract from your target track

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Joining an academically prestigious advisor who discourages internships
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You systematically miss the internship pipeline that is the primary entry mechanism for top industry research labs — no matter how good your publications are
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who believe publication quality alone will open industry research doors, not realizing internship relationships often precede and enable those hires

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Choosing a high-ranked program primarily for ranking
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If the advisor at that program has no industry connections, a rank-10 program placement can underperform a rank-30 program with an advisor who has active Google DeepMind or OpenAI relationships
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Industry-track students who conflate program prestige with advisor-specific industry pipeline access

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Pursuing a PhD to improve SWE job prospects
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You may be filtered as overqualified for some SWE roles, and companies expect higher compensation to justify hiring a PhD SWE — creating a hiring disadvantage on top of the $500K+ opportunity cost
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who assume a PhD universally increases competitiveness across all tech roles, not realizing the premium is concentrated in research-specific roles

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Academic-track PhD without a postdoc plan
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The realistic path to a tenure-track faculty position includes 1–3 years as a postdoc at $55K–$80K/year after 5–7 years of PhD — total timeline to first faculty salary can be 8–10 years
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who see the $120K–$180K first-year faculty salary without accounting for the postdoc bridge years that precede it

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Industry research track PhD without verifying advisor's actual placement record
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: An advisor who claims industry connections but has only placed students at product-team roles (not research labs) provides significantly less value for a research scientist career goal
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who conflate 'students went to industry' with 'students went to top industry research positions' — the distinction between SWE/product roles and research scientist roles is large

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Defaulting to a standard university PhD when a co-supervision program exists at your target lab
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You forego supplemented compensation, faster publication timelines, applied research relevance, and direct relationships with your target employer's researchers
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who are unaware that formal co-supervision programs exist and apply only through traditional university admission channels

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying to PhD programs without distinguishing academic vs. industry track optimization
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Most publicly available PhD advice assumes a single academic track; students don't realize the two tracks require different advisor selection, program evaluation, and application strategy
failure_patterns.consequence: Students end up in programs optimized for the wrong track — e.g., with an academic-oriented advisor who discourages internships when they want an industry research career
warning_signs: Student says 'I want to go into industry eventually' but is evaluating advisors primarily by h-index and publications
Student prioritizes program ranking above advisor-specific placement history for an industry research goal

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating 'went to industry' as equivalent to 'got a research scientist role at a top lab'
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students don't distinguish between SWE/product placements and research scientist placements when reviewing an advisor's student outcomes
failure_patterns.consequence: Student joins a program with an advisor whose 'industry placements' are all SWE roles, not research roles — misaligned with research scientist career goal
warning_signs: Student accepts vague claims like 'my students go to Google and Meta' without asking which teams or roles
Student doesn't search LinkedIn to verify actual job titles of past PhD graduates

failure_patterns.pattern: Pursuing a PhD with a SWE career goal
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students believe a PhD signals competence and increases hiring probability broadly; they don't calculate opportunity cost or understand that PhD premium is role-specific
failure_patterns.consequence: $500K–$600K opportunity cost with marginal or negative return for SWE roles; possible 'overqualified' filter at some companies
warning_signs: Student says 'I want to work at Google/Meta as an engineer and the PhD will help me get in'
Student has not considered that new grad SWE compensation already exceeds PhD stipend by 4–5x

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming program rank is the dominant variable for all career outcomes
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Program rankings are highly visible and easy to compare; advisor-specific variables like internship pipeline and industry connections are opaque and require active research
failure_patterns.consequence: Students at high-ranked programs with academically-oriented advisors get outcompeted for industry research roles by students from lower-ranked programs with strong industry advisor pipelines
warning_signs: Student's primary evaluation criterion is US News or CSRankings position
Student has not asked any prospective advisor where their last 5 graduates went

failure_patterns.pattern: Not investigating co-supervision programs before applying to standard PhD programs
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: These programs are relatively new (post-2020) and not widely discussed in standard PhD application guides; students apply through familiar university-only channels
failure_patterns.consequence: Students miss structurally superior arrangements that offer supplemented compensation, applied research relevance, and direct employer relationships
warning_signs: Student's target employer is a major AI lab but student is only researching standard university admissions
Student has not searched whether their target lab has a formal PhD or residency program

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your actual target role — faculty position, research scientist at an AI lab, applied scientist, or software engineer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student needs academic-track or industry-track optimization, or whether a PhD is appropriate at all
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If faculty: Are you targeting top-5 research universities or are you open to a range? This determines how much program rank should dominate your decision.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If SWE: Have you calculated the opportunity cost of 4–5 years at stipend vs. market salary, and do you understand the PhD premium is marginal or negative for SWE roles?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you looked up the last 5 PhD graduates of your prospective advisor on LinkedIn to see where they actually work and in what roles?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is evaluating advisors on verifiable placement reality vs. claimed reputation or h-index
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the ratio of research scientist vs. SWE/product roles? Are those research roles at top labs (Google Brain, OpenAI, FAIR) or at less prominent research positions?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: This is the single most actionable research step — do this before accepting any offer; claimed connections vs. verifiable placement history are very different signals.

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you directly asked your prospective advisor what their philosophy on student internships is?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the advisor is academic-track or industry-track oriented, and whether they will actively support or passively obstruct internship access
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Did they name specific companies proactively, or were they vague or discouraging? Specificity signals real pipeline; vagueness or discouragement signals academic-track orientation.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask this question explicitly — it is the single clearest diagnostic of advisor track orientation and should not be inferred indirectly

diagnostic_questions.question: What subfield of CS are you targeting, and have you mapped the industry vs. academic job market specifically for that subfield?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student understands that ML/AI, systems, NLP, theory, HCI, security, and databases have meaningfully different industry demand and academic competitiveness profiles
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: For ML/AI: Are you aware that the academic job market is dominated by top-5 programs, or are you relying on a lower-ranked program for a faculty goal?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Theory and HCI have moderate industry demand; ML/AI/NLP have extreme demand. Career strategy should be calibrated to the specific subfield, not CS broadly.

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you researched whether your target industry employer has a formal co-supervision or PhD residency program?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student is aware of the third track — industry co-supervised PhD — and whether they are applying through the optimal channel for their goals
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you compared the co-supervision program's research scope, compensation supplement, and publication culture against the standard university PhD programs you're considering?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Google, Meta AI, Microsoft Research, and OpenAI have formal programs post-2020 — research these before defaulting to standard university admission

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you targeting an academic faculty position, and if so, are you applying to top-10 programs in your subfield?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student's program selection is consistent with the top-heavy reality of academic hiring — rank-20 to rank-20 faculty placement is achievable; rank-20 to MIT is not
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Within top-10 programs, are you selecting advisors with track records of placing students in faculty positions in the last 3 years specifically?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If targeting academia from a lower-ranked program, the student should explicitly assess whether their subfield has exceptions to the top-heaviness pattern

industry_realities.common_belief: A PhD universally improves your competitiveness in tech hiring
industry_realities.actual_reality: The PhD premium is real and substantial only for research scientist and applied scientist roles; for SWE, data engineering, most PM tracks, and management tracks, the premium is marginal or negative
industry_realities.implication: Students should identify their specific target role before pursuing a PhD — not assume it improves all career options

industry_realities.common_belief: Program ranking is the dominant variable in PhD outcome quality
industry_realities.actual_reality: For industry research track, a rank-30 program with an advisor who actively places students at Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Meta AI can outperform a rank-10 program whose advisor has no industry relationships
industry_realities.implication: Industry-track students should weight advisor-specific placement history and industry connections more heavily than aggregate program rank

industry_realities.common_belief: The academic faculty path takes 5–7 years and then you get a faculty job
industry_realities.actual_reality: Most CS faculty positions require a postdoc (1–3 years at $55K–$80K) after the PhD — total timeline to first faculty salary is often 8–10 years
industry_realities.implication: Students planning for academic careers should model the full timeline including postdoc years when evaluating the financial and career trajectory

industry_realities.common_belief: If a PhD advisor says their students 'go to industry,' that means they have strong industry research placement
industry_realities.actual_reality: Industry placements range from SWE/product roles to top AI lab research scientist positions — these are vastly different outcomes that advisors routinely conflate in their claims
industry_realities.implication: Always ask specifically about research scientist placements at named top labs, not just general 'industry' placements; verify on LinkedIn

industry_realities.common_belief: The standard PhD application process is the only path into industry research labs
industry_realities.actual_reality: Since ~2020, major AI labs have established formal co-supervision programs, residency programs, and PhD fellowships — these are structurally distinct tracks with supplemented compensation and applied research
industry_realities.implication: Students targeting specific industry labs should research and apply to these programs directly before defaulting to standard university PhD applications

industry_realities.common_belief: Teaching assistant experience is universally valuable in a PhD program
industry_realities.actual_reality: TA experience is an asset on the academic track and a neutral-to-irrelevant factor on the industry research track — the time cost of TAing is a real tradeoff against research output
industry_realities.implication: Industry-track students should assess whether TA requirements in their program compete with internship time or research output

industry_realities.common_belief: PhD compensation eventually catches up with industry SWE compensation
industry_realities.actual_reality: The stipend-to-industry-SWE gap during the PhD represents $500K–$600K in pretax foregone earnings over 4–5 years, and PhD SWEs and MS SWEs are paid identically at the same level at most companies
industry_realities.implication: The financial calculus only favors the PhD for roles where a PhD is a hard requirement (research scientist) or provides a structural premium — not for general engineering roles

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How to evaluate a prospective advisor
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Looks up advisor's h-index, publication count, and program ranking; treats high citation count as primary signal of advisor quality
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Searches LinkedIn for past PhD students; asks directly about internship placements, specific company names, and the ratio of academic vs. industry research vs. product placements in the last 3 years
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Academic metrics predict academic-track outcomes, not industry research placement — using the wrong evaluation criteria leads to joining a mismatched advisor

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How to think about program ranking
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Uses ranking as a proxy for all quality dimensions — assumes higher rank means better outcomes across all career tracks
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Disaggregates ranking by track: weights rank heavily for academic placements, weights advisor-specific industry connections heavily for industry research placements, recognizes rank is not the dominant variable for industry track
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Optimizing for rank on the industry track causes students to overlook rank-30 advisors with superior industry pipelines

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding what 'went to industry' means in a placement claim
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Accepts 'my students go to Google and Meta' as evidence of strong industry research placement
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Asks 'which teams and roles?' and distinguishes between research scientist positions at Google Brain/FAIR vs. SWE/product team placements — treats these as categorically different outcomes
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Conflating SWE placements with research scientist placements leads to joining an advisor who cannot actually help you reach your research career goal

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How to evaluate the PhD decision itself
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Assumes a PhD broadly improves career prospects in tech; views it as a credential that opens more doors than it closes
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Calculates opportunity cost explicitly, maps the PhD premium by specific role type, recognizes that the premium is concentrated in research roles and marginal or negative for SWE — makes the PhD decision conditional on the target role
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Pursuing a PhD for a SWE goal costs $500K+ in opportunity cost with no meaningful return

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Knows only the standard university PhD application process; applies through university portals and targets advisors at ranked programs
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Is aware of co-supervision programs, industry lab residencies, and formal PhD fellowships at target employers; evaluates these against standard PhD programs before deciding on application strategy
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Missing the co-supervision track means foregoing supplemented compensation, faster timelines, and direct employer relationships that are structurally superior for certain industry research goals

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How to interpret the advisor internship conversation
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Asks about internships as a lifestyle question ('will I have time to intern?') rather than a placement pipeline question
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Uses the internship question as a diagnostic to immediately classify the advisor as academic-track or industry-track oriented; listens for specificity of company names vs. vagueness or discouragement as the key signal
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: An advisor who discourages internships is a structural disadvantage for industry research placement — this should be a near-disqualifying factor for industry-track students
